title: Gyárfás–Sumner Conjecture (Conjecture 1)
statement_text: For every integer $k$ and tree $T$, there is an integer $f(k, T)$ such that every graph with chromatic number at least $f(k, T)$ contains either a clique of size $k$, or an induced copy of $T$.
context_text: Gyárfás and Sumner independently conjectured that for any tree $T$, the class $\mathrm{Forb}(T)$ is $\chi$-bounded. This is described as a 'beautiful and difficult conjecture' and serves as the central motivation for the paper's extension to oriented graphs.
paper_contribution: Proves extensions to oriented graphs: for every oriented star $S$, every oriented graph with sufficiently large chromatic number contains either a transitive tournament $TT_3$ or $S$ as an induced subdigraph (Theorem 15), and establishes positive and negative $\chi$-boundedness results for classes of oriented graphs forbidding subsets of orientations of $P_4$.

title: Conjecture 2
statement_text: $\mathrm{Forb}(H)$ is $\chi$-bounded if and only if $H$ is a forest.
context_text: Here graphs are undirected. For a graph $H$, $\mathrm{Forb}(H)$ is the class of graphs with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$, and a class of graphs is $\chi$-bounded if there is a function $f$ such that $\chi(G)\le f(\omega(G))$ for every $G$ in the class. The Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture states that for every integer $k$ and tree $T$ there is $f(k,T)$ such that every graph with chromatic number at least $f(k,T)$ contains a clique of size $k$ or an induced copy of $T$, i.e. $\mathrm{Forb}(T)$ is $\chi$-bounded for every tree $T$. The authors note that an easy argument shows it is equivalent to the present statement. The 'only if' direction is known: by Erdős' theorem there are graphs of arbitrarily large girth and chromatic number, so $\mathrm{Forb}(H)$ is not $\chi$-bounded when $H$ contains a cycle. The conjecture is known for stars (Ramsey's theorem), paths (Gyárfás) and trees of radius two (Kierstead and Penrice), among others. The paper studies extensions to oriented graphs, where one forbids only some orientations of a tree.
notes: PDF source — math may be garbled. Stated by the paper authors as a reformulation equivalent to the Gyárfás–Sumner Conjecture; no separate citation in the header.

title: Conjecture 4
context_text: Oriented graphs are digraphs with no loops and no digons (orientations of simple graphs); their chromatic number and clique number are those of the underlying graph. For a set $\mathcal{H}$ of oriented graphs, $\mathrm{Forb}(\mathcal{H})$ is the class of oriented graphs containing no member of $\mathcal{H}$ as an induced subdigraph, and a class is $\chi$-bounded if there is a function $f$ with $\chi(G)\le f(\omega(G))$ for every member $G$. $\mathrm{Or}(H)$ denotes the set of orientations of $H$, so $\mathrm{Forb}(\mathrm{Or}(T))$ is just the class of (orientations of) $T$-free graphs. An oriented star is an orientation of $K_{1,n}$; $S_{k,\ell}$ denotes the oriented star on $k+\ell+1$ vertices whose centre has in-degree $k$ and out-degree $\ell$. This conjecture extends to oriented graphs the (known) undirected fact that $\mathrm{Forb}(K_{1,t})$ is $\chi$-bounded. By directional duality and monotonicity it suffices to prove it for $S_{k,k}$ for all $k$; the cases $k=0$ and $k=\ell=1$ were known. Equivalently, for every $p$, $\mathrm{Forb}(\mathrm{Or}(K_p)\cup\{S\})$ (no tournament on $p$ vertices and no induced $S$) has bounded chromatic number. The authors determine $\chi(\mathrm{Forb}(\vec{C}_3,TT_3,S))$ exactly, where $\vec{C}_3$ is the directed triangle and $TT_3$ the transitive tournament on three vertices; Kierstead and Rödl proved that $\mathrm{Forb}(\vec{C}_3,S)$ is $\chi$-bounded, and the authors prove that $\mathrm{Forb}(TT_3,S)$ has bounded chromatic number for every oriented star $S$. The next step would be $\mathrm{Forb}(\mathrm{Or}(K_4)\cup\{S\})$.

title: Conjecture 5
statement_text: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a non-empty subset of $\mathrm{Or}(P_4)$. If $\mathcal{P} \neq \{P^+(3)\}$ and $\mathcal{P} \neq \{P^+(1,1,1)\}$, then $\mathrm{Forb}(\mathcal{P})$ is $\chi$-bounded.
context_text: Oriented graphs are digraphs with no loops and no digons (orientations of simple graphs); their chromatic number and clique number are those of the underlying graph. For a set $\mathcal{H}$ of oriented graphs, $\mathrm{Forb}(\mathcal{H})$ is the class of oriented graphs containing no member of $\mathcal{H}$ as an induced subdigraph, and a class is $\chi$-bounded if there is a function $f$ with $\chi(G)\le f(\omega(G))$ for every member $G$. $\mathrm{Or}(H)$ denotes the set of orientations of $H$, so $\mathrm{Forb}(\mathrm{Or}(T))$ is just the class of (orientations of) $T$-free graphs. $P_4$ is the path on four vertices; it has four orientations up to isomorphism: $P^+(3)$ is the directed path $a\to b\to c\to d$, $P^+(2,1)$ is $a\to b\to c\leftarrow d$, $P^-(2,1)$ is $a\leftarrow b\leftarrow c\to d$, and $P^+(1,1,1)$ is $a\to b\leftarrow c\to d$. Since $P_4$-free graphs (cographs) are perfect, $\mathrm{Forb}(\mathrm{Or}(P_4))$ is $\chi$-bounded. Kierstead and Trotter showed that $\mathrm{Forb}(P^+(3))$ is not $\chi$-bounded, and orientations of shift graphs show that $\mathrm{Forb}(P^+(1,1,1))$ is not $\chi$-bounded. The conjecture asserts these are the only obstructions among non-empty sets of orientations of $P_4$. The authors prove it when $P^+(3)\in\mathcal{P}$: $\mathrm{Forb}(P^+(3),P^+(2,1))$, $\mathrm{Forb}(P^+(3),P^-(2,1))$ and $\mathrm{Forb}(P^+(3),P^+(1,1,1))$ are $\chi$-bounded. Known partial results for the remaining cases include that $\mathrm{Forb}(\vec{C}_3,P^+(2,1))$ is $\chi$-bounded (Kierstead and Rödl), and the authors show $\chi(\mathrm{Forb}(\vec{C}_3,TT_3,P^+(2,1)))=3$ and $\chi(\mathrm{Forb}(TT_3,P^+(2,1)))=4$.
notes: PDF source — math may be garbled. Preceded by the informal statement 'We believe that $\{P^+(3)\}$ and $\{P^+(1,1,1)\}$ are the only non-empty subsets $\mathcal{P}$ of $\mathrm{Or}(P_4)$ such that $\mathrm{Forb}(\mathcal{P})$ is not $\chi$-bounded.'
